title: Latitude Degree Distance Calculator
description: Convert a latitude-degree difference into north-south distance with the Latitude Degree Distance Calculator — mid-latitude aware. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a site spanning 40.0° to 40.9° of latitude covers 0.9 degrees — about 100 km north to south, the calculator's one-line verdict.
quick_answer: The Latitude Degree Distance Calculator converts a latitude-degree difference into north-south distance, applying WGS84's degree length at the span's own latitude. Enter the degree difference and where it sits, and read the distance in kilometres or miles — the dedicated instrument for latitude spans, sibling to the general degrees-to-kilometres page.
steps_intro: Latitude spans, converted at their own latitude:

body.t: A research area defined by latitudes gets its true height here — report it in kilometres, not degrees, and reviewers relax.
The meridian component of a journey, isolated: how much of the trip was pure northing.
A dataset's stated latitude extent cross-checked against its claimed size — one subtraction and this conversion is the audit.
Each 1° band is ~111 km of climate — storm tracks and growing zones sized in degrees become kilometres of reality here.

examples.label: Example · The span matters where it sits

body.t: 0.9° of latitude at 40°N = 99.9 km; the same 0.9° at the equator = 99.5 km. Small differences — but this calculator exists so you never have to call them zero.
Pole to pole is 180° and about 20,003 km of meridian — the half-circumference whose near-twin (the equator's 40,075 km) measures the Earth's flattening by their difference.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
North-south ground distance for a latitude-degree difference, using the WGS84 meridional degree length at the stated latitude.
Do I need an account?
No — degrees and latitude in, distance out.
Can I rely on this for professional work?
The geometry is ellipsoid-true — for planning, reporting and checking, yes. Legal measurement follows survey practice, as everywhere on this site.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84, the frame web maps and GPS share — tile and pixel systems on this page are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — pixels and tiles quantise the world; extra coordinate decimals beyond the cell size are decoration.
How is it different from the Degrees Latitude page?
Same physics, different doorway: that page converts degrees generally; this one is framed around a difference between two latitudes. Use whichever matches your input's shape.
Long spans (10°+)?
Apply the mid-latitude rate, or split the span — degree length drifts ~1% across the whole quadrant, so even the simple approach errs by metres per hundred kilometres.
Crossing the equator?
The difference is still just degrees; use the mid-latitude (≈0) rate. Signs handle hemispheres.
Feet or yards?
Kilometres and miles are the working pair; survey chains remain a romance for other pages.
Longitude instead?
A different, latitude-hungry conversion — the Longitude Degree Distance Calculator owns it.
